newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan March foreign currency deposits fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan March foreign currency deposits fall.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign currency deposits outstanding in commercial banks fell to T$333.9 billion at the end of March from February's T$335.9 billion, the Commercial Times newspaper reported on Sunday.
The paper quoted the central bank as saying the main reason for the fall was that investors withdrew their foreign currency deposits to buy Taiwan dollars to invest in the bullish stock market.
The Taiwan stock index has risen more than 80 percent since February 1996, when the market was beset by tension between Taiwan and rival China. It surged 25 percent in 1997 alone.
The bank also attributed the fall partly to profit-taking on U.S. dollars after the greenback appreciated against the Taiwan dollar in March, the newspaper said.

The figures has stayed high recently because exporters have gradually started to pay for their imported raw materials using foreign currency, instead of Taiwan dollars as before, as they gain more experience with its use, central bank officials said.

Foreign currency deposits grew sharply from June 1995's T$123.97 billion to July's T$130.12 billion and August's T$168.41 billion after China launched a series of missile tests near the island in July and August 1995 to warn Taiwan not to advocate independence, officials said.

China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, also conducted wargames near the island in March 1996 to warn Taiwan residents not to vote for independence in the elections, further triggering surges in foreign currency deposits.
During that period investors transfered their money to foreign currency holdings, but the money remained in Taiwan, central bank officials had said.
